title: Undoable column-resize and density composition guidelines
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Users adjusting column widths in very wide virtualized tables frequently overshoot desired sizes, and current interactions feel brittle in mixed-density UIs. We lack a stable, documented approach to compose density tokens (row height, vertical padding, font scales) with transient resize states and product-level telemetry to detect regressions. This ticket defines the UX and token-level guidelines for an undoable column-resize interaction and a composable density system that plays nicely with virtualization and accessibility requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens defined: density.xs / density.sm / density.md / density.lg map to rowHeight, cellPadding, compactTypographyScale, and hitArea delta
A consistent transient resize state is implemented: overlay guide, live-preview (without reflowing entire viewport), and commit on pointerup
Undo behavior: single-step Ctrl/Cmd+Z (or UI toast ‘Undo’) reverts last committed resize; telemetry events emitted for resize_start, resize_commit, resize_undo
Keyboard affordances: Alt+Arrow and Shift+Alt+Arrow change column width in discrete steps and are announced to screen readers
Virtualization contract: resizing does not force full remeasure; placeholder heuristics for offscreen cells and a debounce mechanism on live-preview
Design tokens and component API documented in the design system spec and a Figma kit updated with token samples and animation timing
design_notes: Principles: 1) Make density composable so teams can mix compact rows with expanded detail rows without surprising layout shifts. 2) Make resize forgiving: transient previews plus an explicit commit step, plus undo. 3) Avoid wide re-renders in virtualized lists: prefer placeholder outlines and incremental remeasure. Interaction details: - Pointer resize: show a thin kinetic guide line and a soft preview region (50ms animation) that updates width while debounced to 60ms for heavy tables. - If a user performs a quick drag then releases, commit occurs immediately; if the user presses Escape before pointerup, roll back to previous width. - Provide a persistent small toast 'Column width updated — Undo' for 5s after commit; toast is dismissible and accessible via keyboard. - Telemetry: emit resize_start (column_key, origin), resize_live_sample (sampled values, sampling_rate=10%), resize_commit (old_width, new_width), resize_rollback, and resize_undo. Use these to compute accidental-resize rate and median commit delta.
decisions: Use a single density token set that composes primitives (rowHeight, verticalPadding, fontScale, controlGap) instead of separate ad-hoc CSS classes
Implement undo as a client-side single-step action tied to the app-level history stack plus a visible toast affordance
Telemetry events names standardized as: table_resize_start, table_resize_preview, table_resize_commit, table_resize_rollback, table_resize_undo
Keyboard step size defaults: 8px per Alt+Arrow press; Shift+Alt accelerates to 32px
Accessibility: announce 'Column resized to X pixels' on commit and expose aria-describedby on the toast for screen readers
next_steps: Sync with Runtime engineers to validate virtualization contract (ENG-2411)
Prototype a small Figma interactive demonstrating transient preview + toast undo
Draft token migration guide for teams using legacy density classes
Create telemetry dashboard spec with metrics: accidental_resizes_rate, median_resize_delta, undo_rate
